nodes.title: Artin vanishing for constructible complexes on affine schemes
nodes.statement: Let k be a separably closed field, n ≥ 1 invertible in k, Λ a noetherian ring with nΛ = 0, and U an affine scheme of finite type over k. (a) Imported, not planned here: for every constructible sheaf F of Λ-modules on U_ét, H^q(U, F) = 0 for q > dim Supp F (Artin's affine vanishing with the support-sensitive bound; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.affineArtinVanishing). (b) Let K ∈ D^b_c(U, Λ) and let d_q ∈ ℤ ∪ {−∞} satisfy dim Supp ℋ^q(K) ≤ d_q for every q (dim ∅ = −∞). Then H^m(U, K) = 0 for every m > max_q (q + d_q). (c) In particular, if dim Supp ℋ^q(K) ≤ −q for all q, then H^m(U, K) = 0 for m > 0; and H^m(U, K) = 0 for m > dim U + max{q : ℋ^q(K) ≠ 0}. (d) The same bounds hold for K ∈ D^b_c(U, O_E) and D^b_c(U, E) (E/ℚ_ℓ finite, ℓ invertible in k). Parts (b)–(d) are the complex and adic forms that the upstream section does not state.
hypotheses: k separably closed; n invertible in k; Λ noetherian with nΛ = 0 (for (a) and (b)).
U affine of finite type over k; affineness is essential: H²(P¹, Λ(1)) = Λ although dim P¹ = 1.

For O_E and E coefficients use EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.1–F.4.5: normalized ℓ-adic systems with cohomological and Tor intervals uniform in the level, their realization, and finite E/ℚ_ℓ through O_E lattices. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: (a) is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3 (VanishingCycles.affineArtinVanishing), which states the constructible bound q > dim Supp F for prime-to-characteristic torsion coefficients; it is the statement of SGA 4 XIV Théorème 3.1 and Corollaire 3.2, restated as BBD Corollaire 4.1.4.

(b) Use the hypercohomology spectral sequence E₂^{p,q} = H^p(U, ℋ^q K) ⇒ H^{p+q}(U, K), which converges because K is bounded. By (a), E₂^{p,q} = 0 for p > d_q, so every term with p + q = m vanishes when m > q + d_q for all q.
(c) is (b) with d_q = −q, respectively d_q = dim U.

(d) For O = ℤ_ℓ, apply (b) to each level ℤ/ℓ^n of the normalized system (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.1). The universal-coefficient sequence puts the support of ℋ^q(K_n) inside the supports of ℋ^q(K) and ℋ^{q+1}(K), and q + d_{q+1} < (q+1) + d_{q+1}, so the levels satisfy the same bound max_q(q + d_q). Pass to the realization: §F.4.2 identifies RΓ of the realization with Rlim of the finite levels; the groups H^{m−1}(U, K_n) are finite (§F.3), so the Milnor lim¹ term vanishes and H^m(U, K) = 0 above the bound. For O = O_E restrict scalars to ℤ_ℓ; rational coefficients follow by inverting ℓ (§F.4.5). The bound is imposed only on nonzero ordinary cohomology sheaves.
acceptance: U = 𝔸¹_k, F constructible: H^q(𝔸¹, F) = 0 for q ≥ 2; the bound is sharp: for n > 1, H¹(𝔾_m, ℤ/n) ≅ ℤ/n(−1) ≠ 0.
K = i_{x*}Λ[−q] for a closed point x: d_q = 0, and H^m(U, K) = 0 for m ≠ q, as (b) predicts.
Non-example: U = P¹ is not affine and H²(P¹, Λ(1)) ≅ Λ, so affineness cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Vanishing of low-degree compactly supported cohomology of smooth affine varieties
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, n invertible in k, Λ = O/π^m (more generally a noetherian self-injective ring killed by n), U a smooth affine k-scheme of pure dimension d and L a locally constant constructible sheaf of Λ-modules on U. Then H^i_c(U, L) = 0 for i < d. The same holds for a lisse O_E-sheaf or a lisse E-sheaf L (E/ℚ_ℓ finite, ℓ invertible in k).
hypotheses: k separably closed, n invertible; U smooth, affine, of pure dimension d.
Λ self-injective, so that Poincaré duality is a perfect pairing degreewise; for O_E use derived duality and the universal-coefficient sequence.

A lisse O_E-sheaf here means locally finite free over O_E; geometric finiteness and coefficient reduction are those of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.4 for O = ℤ_ℓ. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: For locally finite-free finite-coefficient L, use smooth purity and finite-Tor Poincaré duality (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.5–F.6). For general lcc L over the stated noetherian self-injective commutative Λ, use the finite-length filtration by powers of its Jacobson radical: the quotient local systems are finite-dimensional over residue fields, where Poincaré duality applies, and compact vanishing passes through the short exact sequences. Such a ring is artinian; self-injectivity also makes its finite-module dual exact and reflexive. This dévissage does not import biduality on arbitrary nonperfect Dbc objects from §F.5, which states it on ctf inputs.

For each residue-field local system in that filtration, Artin vanishing (EDC.4/affine-vanishing-hypercohomology (a)) gives H^{2d−i}(U,L^∨(d)) = 0 when 2d−i > d. Field-coefficient Poincaré duality then gives H^i_c(U,L) = 0 for i < d; dévissage gives the stated Λ case.

For O use derived Poincaré duality and the universal-coefficient short exact sequence. The Hom term uses H^{2d−i}; the Ext-one term uses H^{2d−i+1}. Both vanish for i < d. Retain the locally finite-free lisse input and geometric finiteness. Tensoring with E gives the rational case.

Cross-check: for finite or rational coefficients L[d] is perverse on the smooth U, and the affine compact-support vanishing H^i_c(U, P) = 0 for i < 0 of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8 gives the same range.
acceptance: U = 𝔸^d: H^i_c(𝔸^d, Λ) = 0 for i ≠ 2d, in particular for i < d.
U = 𝔾_m (d = 1): H⁰_c(𝔾_m, Λ) = 0 while H¹_c(𝔾_m, Λ) = Λ ≠ 0 for nonzero Λ — the bound i < d is sharp.
Non-example: U = P¹ − ∅ is not affine and H⁰_c(P¹, Λ) = Λ ≠ 0 although d = 1.

sources.match: Deligne deduces the vanishing of H^i_c(X − Y) for i < n from affine vanishing and Poincaré duality on the smooth affine X − Y.

§F.5 states exceptional inverse image and duality, §F.6 smooth purity f^!Λ ≅ Λ(d)[2d] and higher-dimensional Poincaré duality; §F.8 states affine vanishing of compactly supported cohomology of perverse objects in negative degrees. The duality input of the first step is imported from there.

nodes.title: The weak Lefschetz theorem
nodes.statement: Let k be a separably closed field, ℓ a prime invertible in k, X a smooth projective k-scheme of pure dimension n + 1 with a closed immersion X ⊂ P^N_k, H ⊂ P^N a hyperplane and Y = X ∩ H (scheme-theoretic, H containing no irreducible component of X), with inclusion i : Y → X. Let Λ be ℤ/ℓ^m, O_E/λ^m, O_E or E (E/ℚ_ℓ finite), and L a locally constant constructible (respectively lisse) sheaf of Λ-modules on X. Then the restriction i^* : H^q(X, L) → H^q(Y, i^*L) is an isomorphism for q < n and injective for q = n. Y need not be smooth. If X, Y and L are defined over a subfield k₀ with k = k₀^sep, i^* is Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant; over k₀ = 𝔽_q it commutes with the geometric Frobenius. For a smooth Y and constant coefficients this is VanishingCycles.etaleWeakLefschetz of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7; the singular sections, the lisse coefficients and the equivariance are what this node adds.
hypotheses: k separably closed; ℓ invertible in k; X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1; Y = X ∩ H for a hyperplane H of an embedding X ⊂ P^N. The hyperplane contains no irreducible component of X.
U := X − Y is affine (a closed subscheme of P^N − H ≅ 𝔸^N) and smooth of pure dimension n + 1; these are the only properties of Y used.

This theorem is distinct from hard Lefschetz (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9) and makes no claim about the nondegeneracy of the intersection form on the vanishing part (EDC.4/vanishing-and-restriction-subspaces).

For O_E coefficients use finite-free lisse sheaves. Integral and rational coefficients are those of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.1–F.4.5 (ℤ_ℓ, ℚ_ℓ and finite E); O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: U = X − Y is affine: X − Y → P^N − H is a closed immersion, hence an affine morphism (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_iff_isAffineHom), into the affine scheme P^N − H = D_+(h) ≅ Spec of a degree-zero localization (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec); so U is affine (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isAffine_of_isAffineHom).

The localization triangle j_!j^*L → L → i_*i^*L → for j : U → X open and i : Y → X closed (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.7, ClassicalAlgebraic.supportLocalization) gives, X being proper, the exact sequence … → H^q_c(U, L) → H^q(X, L) → H^q(Y, i^*L) → H^{q+1}_c(U, L) → … (compact-support localization, §§0.8 and F.2.5).
By EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine applied to the smooth affine U of pure dimension n + 1, H^q_c(U, L) = 0 for q < n + 1. Hence i^* is injective for q ≤ n and surjective for q ≤ n − 1.

Equivariance: all maps are induced by morphisms of schemes defined over k₀, hence commute with the Galois action; the action and the Frobenius conventions are those of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.6 (VanishingCycles.adicFunctoriality) and §F.10.2b (VanishingCycles.frobeniusCohomology).
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n a hyperplane: i^* : H^q(P^{n+1}, Λ) → H^q(P^n, Λ) is an isomorphism for q ≤ 2n (the P^m calculation of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9), consistent with the theorem.
X = P¹ × P¹ ⊂ P³ (n + 1 = 2), Y a smooth conic: i^* is injective on H¹ = 0 and an isomorphism on H⁰; on H² (outside the range) the map Λ(−1)² → Λ(−1) is not injective, so the range q ≤ n is sharp.
n + 1 = 1 (X a smooth projective curve, Y a finite set of points): H⁰(X) → H⁰(Y) is injective.

Agreement with the upstream statement: for Y smooth and L = Λ constant, the conclusion is that of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7 (VanishingCycles.etaleWeakLefschetz), whose plane-cubic check H¹(P²) = 0 → H¹(C) = Λ² is injective and not surjective.

sources.match: Deligne's weak Lefschetz: the long exact sequence of relative cohomology together with the vanishing of H^i_c(X − Y) for i ≤ n gives the restriction statement.
Weil I derives weak Lefschetz from affine vanishing and Poincaré duality, exactly the route of this node.

§F.7 states weak Lefschetz for a smooth ample hyperplane section of a smooth projective variety with finite or ℓ-adic constant coefficients; §0.7 states the open–closed localization triangles used in the second step.

nodes.title: The dual (Gysin) form of weak Lefschetz
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz assume moreover that Y is smooth (a smooth hyperplane section, of pure dimension n). Then the Gysin map i_* : H^q(Y, i^*L) → H^{q+2}(X, L(1)) is an isomorphism for q > n and surjective for q = n, for Λ = ℤ/ℓ^m, O_E/λ^m, O_E or E and L locally constant constructible (lisse). Equivalently H^{q+2}(X, L(1))/i_*H^q(Y, i^*L) injects into H^{q+2}(U, L(1)), which vanishes for q + 2 > n + 1.
hypotheses: As in EDC.4/weak-lefschetz, with Y smooth of pure dimension n (smooth pair (Y, X) of codimension 1).
proofSteps: The Gysin sequence of the smooth pair (Y, X): apply cohomology to the localization triangle i_*i^!L → L → Rj_*j^*L of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.7 and identify i^!L ≅ i^*L(−1)[−2] by smooth-pair purity (§0.10, ClassicalAlgebraic.smoothBoundaryPurity, and its adic form in §F.6, VanishingCycles.smoothPairGysin). This gives … → H^{q+1}(U, L(1)) → H^q(Y, i^*L) →i_* H^{q+2}(X, L(1)) → H^{q+2}(U, L(1)) → ….
U = X − Y is affine of dimension n + 1, so H^m(U, L(1)) = 0 for m > n + 1 (EDC.4/affine-vanishing-hypercohomology (a)).
Hence i_* is surjective when q + 2 > n + 1 (q ≥ n) and injective when q + 1 > n + 1 (q > n).

For field coefficients this is the transpose of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz under Poincaré duality on X and Y (the Gysin map is the transpose of i^*, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6), which gives the same ranges.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n: i_* : H^q(P^n) → H^{q+2}(P^{n+1})(1) sends h^j to h^{j+1}; it is an isomorphism for n < q ≤ 2n and surjective for q = n.
n = 0: Y a finite set of d ≥ 1 distinct geometric points on a smooth connected projective curve X; i_* : H⁰(Y) = Λ^d → H²(X, Λ(1)) = Λ is the sum map, surjective.
The range is sharp: for X = P¹ × P¹ and Y a conic, i_* : H⁰(Y) → H²(X)(1) is not surjective onto Λ² (q = 0 < n = 1).

sources.match: Deligne states the Gysin (dual) form of weak Lefschetz.
Weil I uses the surjectivity of the Gysin map H^{n−1}(Y)(−1) → H^{n+1}(X) as the dual of weak Lefschetz.

§0.10 states smooth-pair purity i^!Λ ≅ Λ_Z(−c)[−2c] with its class, and §F.6 the Gysin maps of smooth pairs with their projection formulas and adic realizations; with the triangle of §0.7 they give the Gysin sequence used here.

nodes.title: Integral weak Lefschetz: torsion-freeness of the cokernel
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz with L = ℤ_ℓ (U = X − Y, n + 1 = dim X): the group H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) is torsion-free, and consequently H^n(Y, ℤ_ℓ)/i^*H^n(X, ℤ_ℓ) is torsion-free. The same holds for O_E in place of ℤ_ℓ.
hypotheses: k separably closed, ℓ invertible; X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1; Y = X ∩ H a hyperplane section; U = X − Y.

RΓ_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) is a perfect complex of ℤ_ℓ-modules with RΓ_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) ⊗^L ℤ/ℓ ≅ RΓ_c(U, ℤ/ℓ): this is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.4 (VanishingCycles.adicFiniteness). O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: Universal coefficients: since RΓ_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) is perfect with derived reduction RΓ_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.4), there is a short exact sequence 0 → H^n_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) ⊗ ℤ/ℓ → H^n_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) → Tor₁^{ℤ_ℓ}(H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ), ℤ/ℓ) → 0.

H^n_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 by EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine (n < n + 1), so H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ)[ℓ] = Tor₁(H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ), ℤ/ℓ) = 0; a finitely generated ℤ_ℓ-module without ℓ-torsion is torsion-free.
The exact sequence H^n(X, ℤ_ℓ) → H^n(Y, ℤ_ℓ) → H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz embeds H^n(Y)/i^*H^n(X) into the torsion-free H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ).
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}: H^{n+1}_c(𝔸^{n+1}, ℤ_ℓ) = 0 (torsion-free) and the cokernel H^n(P^n)/H^n(P^{n+1}) = 0.
X a smooth projective surface (n = 1) with Y a smooth hyperplane curve: H¹(Y, ℤ_ℓ)/i^*H¹(X, ℤ_ℓ) is a free ℤ_ℓ-module (the vanishing part of the curve's H¹ is saturated).

Affineness diagnostic: U = P¹ is smooth of dimension one but non-affine, and H⁰_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) = ℤ/ℓ ≠ 0. Thus smoothness alone does not supply the compact-vanishing input used by the universal-coefficient argument.

sources.match: Deligne's (4.1.6): the universal coefficient formula gives the torsion-freeness of H^{n+1}_c(X − Y, ℤ_ℓ), hence of H^n(Y, ℤ_ℓ)/H^n(X, ℤ_ℓ).

States finite generation over ℤ_ℓ, bounded perfect RΓ and RΓ_c, and the derived reduction RΓ_c(X, K_ℤℓ) ⊗^L ℤ/ℓ^n ≅ RΓ_c(X, K_n) for separated finite-type schemes over a separably closed field; this is the hypothesis of the first step.

nodes.title: Weak Lefschetz for ample divisors and hypersurface sections
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, ℓ invertible in k, X a smooth projective k-scheme of pure dimension n + 1, ℒ an ample invertible O_X-module, r ≥ 1 and s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ^{⊗r}) nonzero on every irreducible component, with effective Cartier zero scheme Y = V(s). Then the conclusions of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (restriction H^q(X, L) → H^q(Y, L) bijective for q < n, injective for q = n) and, when Y is smooth, of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-gysin hold, for Λ = ℤ/ℓ^m, O_E/λ^m, O_E, E. In particular they hold for Y = X ∩ V(F) with F a homogeneous form of degree r on P^N ⊃ X. By induction they hold along a chain X = X_0 ⊃ X_1 ⊃ … ⊃ X_c of smooth successive ample divisors.
hypotheses: X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1 over k separably closed; ℒ ample; Y the zero scheme of a section of a positive power of ℒ. The section is nonzero on every irreducible component, so Y is an effective Cartier divisor.
Only the affineness of X − Y = X_s and its smoothness are used, together with topological invariance of the étale site (Y and Y_red have the same cohomology; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.4).
proofSteps: X is proper over k and ℒ^{⊗r} is ample, so X_s = X − Y is affine (Stacks, Tag 0EKE: for f universally closed and ℒ f-ample, X_s → S is affine; requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0). Ampleness alone does not suffice without properness: on a quasi-affine non-affine X with ℒ = O_X and s = 1, X_s = X.

With U = X_s affine and smooth of pure dimension n + 1, the proofs of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz and EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-gysin apply verbatim: they use only EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine and EDC.4/affine-vanishing-hypercohomology for U.

Alternatively, ℒ^{⊗rN} is very ample for N ≫ 0 and s^N is a hyperplane section in the corresponding embedding; Y and V(s^N) have the same reduced subscheme, and étale cohomology depends only on it (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.4, VanishingCycles.universalHomeomorphismEtaleEquivalence). For F of degree r on P^N, V(F) is a hyperplane section of the r-th Veronese re-embedding (Weil I, 5.7; the re-embedding is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0).
Chains: apply the statement to each X_{j+1} ⊂ X_j (each smooth projective) and compose.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y a smooth quadric hypersurface (r = 2): H^q(Y) ≅ H^q(P^{n+1}) for q < n.
n + 1 = 2, X = P², Y a smooth plane cubic curve: H⁰(P²) → H⁰(Y) is an isomorphism (q = 0 < n = 1) and H¹(P²) = 0 → H¹(Y) = Λ² is injective.

Non-example: take X = P¹ × P¹ and ℒ = O(0,2), nef but not ample, with s vanishing at two distinct points of the second factor. Then Y is the disjoint union of two fibres and H⁰(X,Λ) = Λ → H⁰(Y,Λ) = Λ² is diagonal, not an isomorphism although 0 < n = 1. The complement P¹ × G_m is non-affine and H¹_c(P¹ × G_m,Λ) = Λ ≠ 0, violating the low-degree compact vanishing required in the proof.

sources.match: Weil I's Veronese re-embedding turns degree-r hypersurface sections into hyperplane sections.
For X proper (universally closed) and ℒ ample, X_s is affine: the complement of an ample divisor in a proper scheme is affine.
States that universal homeomorphisms induce equivalences of étale sites with transport of sheaves and cohomology; used to replace Y by its reduction.

nodes.title: Cohomology of smooth complete intersections
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, ℓ invertible in k, and X ⊂ P^N_k a smooth complete intersection of dimension m ≥ 1 (there is a chain P^N = X_N ⊃ X_{N−1} ⊃ … ⊃ X_m = X with each X_r = X_{r+1} ∩ H_r for a hypersurface H_r, all X_r smooth). Let Λ = ℤ/ℓ^a, ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ and h = c₁(O(1))|_X ∈ H²(X, Λ(1)). Then: (a) for q ≠ m, 0 ≤ q ≤ 2m, H^q(X, Λ) = 0 for q odd and H^q(X, Λ(q/2)) is free of rank one for q even; h^{q/2} generates for q < m. For q > m, a generator is dual to h^{m−q/2} under Poincaré duality, and h^{q/2} is deg(X) times that generator (after the trace normalization); the restriction H^q(P^N, Λ) → H^q(X, Λ) is an isomorphism for q < m. (b) H^m(X, Λ) = Λ(−m/2)·h^{m/2} ⊕ H^m(X, Λ)_0 when m is even (for Λ = ℚ_ℓ, and for ℤ/ℓ^a or ℤ_ℓ when deg X is prime to ℓ), with H^m(X)_0 := ker(∪h : H^m(X) → H^{m+2}(X)(1)); H^m(X) = H^m(X)_0 when m is odd. (c) With ℤ_ℓ coefficients all H^q(X, ℤ_ℓ) are torsion-free. (d) If X is defined over 𝔽_q, the geometric Frobenius acts on H^{2j}(X, ℚ_ℓ), 2j ≠ m, by multiplication by q^j. The comparison of primitive ranks across characteristics is the separate target EDC.6/complete-intersection-betti-comparison; it is not a conclusion of this node.
hypotheses: X a smooth complete intersection in P^N over a separably closed field; ℓ invertible.
The splitting in (b) uses that h^m has degree deg X on X (Tr(h^m) = deg X): it is a direct sum over ℚ_ℓ, and over ℤ/ℓ^a or ℤ_ℓ only when deg X is a unit.
proofSteps: Induction along the chain X_N = P^N ⊃ … ⊃ X_m = X, each X_r an ample divisor in the smooth projective X_{r+1} (EDC.4/ample-divisor-weak-lefschetz): H^q(X_{r+1}) → H^q(X_r) is bijective for q < r and injective for q = r; the Gysin map H^q(X_r)(−1) → H^{q+2}(X_{r+1}) is bijective for q > r and surjective for q = r (EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-gysin).

Hence H^q(X) ≅ H^q(P^N) for q < m, where H^*(P^N) has one Λ(−i) in each even degree 2i generated by the hyperplane powers (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9 and the first check of §F.7), and by Poincaré duality on X (§§F.5–F.6, with the adic realization of §F.4.4) H^q(X) for q > m is dual to H^{2m−q}(X), which is Λ·h^{m−q/2} or 0.

Torsion-freeness: for each smooth divisor X_r in X_{r+1}, integral weak Lefschetz (EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-integral) gives an injection H^r(X_{r+1}, ℤ_ℓ) → H^r(X_r, ℤ_ℓ) with torsion-free cokernel. The source group is in a degree below dim X_{r+1}, hence identified with the free projective-space group by the already proved low-degree calculation. Therefore the middle group of X_r is free as well. Integral Poincaré duality and its universal-coefficient sequence then give freeness in all higher degrees, including degree r+1. This avoids assuming freeness in degree r+1 to prove it in degree r.

Splitting (b): Tr_X(h^m) = deg X (the degree of the hyperplane class on X, from the point normalization of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9 and the projection formula of §F.6), so h^{m/2} ∪ h^{m/2} ≠ 0 and Λh^{m/2} is a direct summand complementary to the kernel of ∪h when deg X is invertible in Λ.

Frobenius: the low-degree hyperplane powers have eigenvalue q^j in untwisted cohomology (geometric Frobenius acts on Λ(1) by q⁻¹, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.10.2b). In high degrees use the perfect Frobenius-equivariant pairing with low degrees, whose multiplier is q^m; the resulting eigenvalue is q^j even when h^j is not an integral generator.
acceptance: X = P^m itself (N = m): H^m(X)_0 = 0 and every statement reduces to the P^m calculation of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9.
X a smooth plane cubic (m = 1): H¹(X, ℚ_ℓ) = H¹(X)_0 has dimension 2 = b_1^0 for degree 3.
X a smooth quadric surface in P³ (m = 2, degree 2): H²(X, ℚ_ℓ(1)) = ℚ_ℓh ⊕ H²_0 with dim H²_0 = 1; with ℤ/2 coefficients the splitting fails (deg X = 2 is not invertible), as the hypothesis requires.
Smooth plane conic with Λ = ℤ/2: H²(X, Λ(1)) ≅ Λ but h = 2[point] = 0. With ℤ₂, h spans an index-two submodule. Thus high-degree freeness must not be stated as generation by h.

The active forms are typed over the common finite-type separated k-base; the carrier data for ample sections and complete-intersection chains are the SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 requests of this packet.

nodes.title: The projective-bundle decomposition: ring structure, pushforward, pairing and Frobenius weights
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with n invertible, Λ = ℤ/n or O/π^r, with bounded constructible K. For Λ = O_E or E require additionally that X is of finite type over a field with ℓ invertible and take bounded constructible K. Let V be a locally free O_X-module of rank m + 1, π : P(V) → X the projective bundle of lines in V and ξ = c₁(O(1)) ∈ H²(P(V), Λ(1)). (a) Imported, not planned here: the map ⊕_{j=0}^{m} Λ_X(−j)[−2j] → Rπ_*Λ_{P(V)} given by ξ^j is an isomorphism (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9, ClassicalAlgebraic.cycleClasses, for finite Λ; its adic realization is §F.7); consequently, by the projection formula, H^q(P(V), π^*K) ≅ ⊕_j H^{q−2j}(X, K(−j)) for every such K. The node adds: (b) ring structure: ⊕_q H^q(P(V), Λ(∗)) = H^∗(X, Λ(∗))[ξ]/(Σ_{r=0}^{m+1} c_r(V) ξ^{m+1−r}); (c) for X smooth over k and π_* the Gysin pushforward (relative dimension m), π_*(π^*a ∪ ξ^j) = 0 for j < m and π_*(π^*a ∪ ξ^m) = a; (d) if X and V are defined over a field k₀ and k = k₀^sep, the decomposition H^q(P(V)_k, Λ) ≅ ⊕_j H^{q−2j}(X_k, Λ)(−j) is Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant; over k₀ = 𝔽_q the geometric Frobenius acts on the j-th summand as F_X ⊗ q^j (untwisted cohomology); (e) for X smooth proper of pure dimension d over k separably closed, the Poincaré pairing on P(V) restricted to the summands j and j' vanishes when j + j' < m and is ⟨π^*a ξ^j, π^*b ξ^{m−j}⟩ = ⟨a, b⟩_X when j + j' = m.
hypotheses: X qcqs with n invertible (for (c) and (e): X smooth, respectively smooth proper, over a field); V locally free of rank m + 1 (Zariski-locally free).

P(V) parametrizes lines in V and ξ = c₁(O(1)), with O(1) dual to the tautological line: this is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.4 (projectiveBundle V := relativeProj of the symmetric algebra of V^∨, with projectiveBundle_dual_convention) on TauCetiRoadmap main; the plus-sign Chern relation follows this convention.
Twists and Frobenius conventions are those of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.3 (etaleTateTwists) and §F.10.2b (geometric Frobenius acts on Λ(−1) by q).

The étale Chern classes c_r(V) of (b) are those of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/chern-classes (defined by the projective-bundle relation); EtaleCohomologyFoundations states c₁ (§0.9) but not the higher étale classes. The adic extension is the realization of §F.7 in its finite-type range; O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: (a) is imported: EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9 states the decomposition for finite Λ with summands generated by powers of c₁(O(1)), compatibly with pullback and coefficient reduction, and §F.7 realizes it adically through §F.4. The cohomological form with coefficients π^*K follows from the projection formula (§F.2.7 for Rf_! = Rf_* along the proper π).
(b) is the definition of the Chern classes by the projective-bundle relation (EDC.3/chern-classes) together with the freeness in (a).

(c) The pushforward π_* along the smooth proper π is the trace of Rπ_! = Rπ_* against π^!Λ ≅ Λ(m)[2m] (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11 and smooth purity, §F.6), and the projection formula (§F.2.7) gives π_*(π^*a ∪ ξ^j) = a ∪ π_*(ξ^j); π_*(ξ^j) ∈ H^{2j−2m}(X) vanishes for j < m by degree and π_*(ξ^m) = 1 because on a fibre P^m, Tr(ξ^m) = 1 (point normalization of §0.9).

(d) ξ is the Chern class of a line bundle defined over k₀, so it is Galois-invariant in H²(P(V)_k, Λ(1)); in untwisted cohomology F^*ξ = q·ξ (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.10.2b: geometric Frobenius acts on Λ(1) by q⁻¹), which gives the stated action.
(e) Tr_{P(V)} = Tr_X ∘ π_* (compatibility of smooth traces with composition, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11, ClassicalAlgebraic.smoothTrace), and (c).
acceptance: X = Spec k for k separably closed, E = k^{m+1}: P(E) = P^m and (a) is H^∗(P^m) = Λ[ξ]/(ξ^{m+1}) (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9).

P¹-bundle over a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over 𝔽_q: the geometric Frobenius has eigenvalues those of H^a(C) and q times those of H^{a−2}(C) on H^a(P(E)); e.g. dim H²(P(E)) = 2 with eigenvalues q, q.
The Frobenius twist on the summand j is q^j, not 1: 'equal Betti numbers' is not enough (the stage forbids merely equating Betti numbers).

Agreement with the upstream statement: on a rank-one bundle P(V) = X and only the j = 0 summand occurs, and the zero bundle has empty projectivization, as in the checks of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9.

nodes.title: Direct images along the blow-up of a smooth centre
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, ℓ invertible in k, X a smooth separated finite-type k-scheme, i : Z → X a smooth closed subscheme of pure codimension c ≥ 2, π : X̃ = Bl_Z X → X the blow-up, E = π^{−1}(Z) the exceptional divisor with j : E → X̃ and p = π|_E : E → Z, and ζ := c₁(O_E(1)) = −j^*c₁(O_X̃(E)) ∈ H²(E, Λ(1)). Then X̃ is smooth, E is a smooth divisor with E ≅ P(N_{Z/X}) over Z (imported), Λ_X → Rπ_*Λ_X̃ is split injective, and Rπ_*Λ_X̃ ≅ Λ_X ⊕ ⊕_{a=1}^{c−1} i_*Λ_Z(−a)[−2a]; equivalently π_*Λ = Λ, R^{2a}π_*Λ ≅ i_*Λ_Z(−a) for 1 ≤ a ≤ c − 1 (generated by the image of ζ^a under j^*), and R^qπ_*Λ = 0 for all other q > 0. Λ = ℤ/ℓ^m, O_E/λ^m, O_E or E. The splitting is the actual sum of the adjunction unit and j_*(zeta^(a-1)p^*(-)); its restriction to E has columns 1,-zeta,...,-zeta^(c-1).
hypotheses: X smooth, separated and of finite type over a field k, Z ⊂ X smooth of pure codimension c ≥ 2; ℓ invertible in k.

The geometry of the blow-up (X̃ smooth, E = P(N_{Z/X}), O_X̃(−E)|_E = O_E(1), π an isomorphism over X − Z, π proper) is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0. TauCetiRoadmap main states blow-ups and strict transforms (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.11 with StableReduction Layer 4) and normal bundles of regular immersions (§5.5), but not this identification of the exceptional divisor.
proofSteps: Over X − Z, π is an isomorphism, so Rπ_*Λ|_{X−Z} = Λ.

π is proper, so proper base change (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.2.1, VanishingCycles.properBaseChange) gives (R^qπ_*Λ)_z̄ = H^q(P^{c−1}_{z̄}, Λ) at geometric points z̄ of Z: Λ(−a) for q = 2a ≤ 2(c − 1), 0 otherwise (EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (a) over a point).

Use the adjunction unit for Λ_X and, for 1 ≤ a ≤ c−1, the morphism i_*Λ_Z(−a)[−2a] → Rπ_*Λ_X̃ obtained from p^*, multiplication by ζ^{a−1}, and the exceptional-divisor Gysin map j_* (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6, VanishingCycles.smoothPairGysin). Their direct sum defines the proposed decomposition morphism.

Check this morphism on geometric stalks by proper base change. Off Z it is the identity. Over Z its restriction to E has columns 1 and −ζ^a, since j^*j_*y = −ζ∪y by the self-intersection formula of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6. These form the projective-bundle basis, so the morphism is an isomorphism. The trace π_* splits its first column by the degree-one projection formula. Merely knowing the cohomology sheaves of a complex would not prove a derived splitting.

Applying RΓ recovers VanishingCycles.etaleBlowup of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7, which states the decomposition of RΓ(Bl_Z X, Λ) with the same exceptional Gysin columns; this node is its sheaf-level form over X, needed for supports and compact supports in EDC.4/pullback-injective-blowup-bundle.
acceptance: Blow-up of a point in a surface (c = 2): R²π_*Λ = Λ_x(−1) at the point x, generated by the class of the exceptional curve.
c = 3, Z a point in a threefold: R²π_*Λ = Λ_x(−1), R⁴π_*Λ = Λ_x(−2), R¹ = R³ = 0.
Non-example: for c = 1 the blow-up is an isomorphism and Rπ_*Λ = Λ; the formula's sum over 1 ≤ a ≤ c − 1 is then empty, so no correction term appears.
The active forms are typed over the common finite-type separated k-base; the exceptional-divisor geometry is the SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 request of this packet.

nodes.title: The blow-up formula along a smooth centre: retraction, traces and Frobenius weights
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.4/blowup-direct-images, for every q the map Φ : H^q(X, Λ) ⊕ ⊕_{a=1}^{c−1} H^{q−2a}(Z, Λ(−a)) → H^q(X̃, Λ), (x, (z_a)) ↦ π^*x + Σ_a j_*(ζ^{a−1} ∪ p^*z_a), where j_* : H^{r}(E, Λ(s)) → H^{r+2}(X̃, Λ(s+1)) is the Gysin map of the divisor E, is an isomorphism; this decomposition with its displayed exceptional Gysin columns and inverse signs is VanishingCycles.etaleBlowup of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7, imported. The node adds the following compatibilities of this specific Φ: its inverse has first component π_* (the Gysin pushforward, with π_*π^* = id); j^*π^*x = p^*i^*x; π_*j_*(ζ^{a−1} ∪ p^*z) = 0 for 1 ≤ a ≤ c − 1 (degree reasons along the fibres P^{c−1}); for X proper over k separably closed, Tr_X̃(π^*x) = Tr_X(x) on top-degree classes; if X, Z are defined over k₀ (k = k₀^sep) Φ is Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant and over 𝔽_q the geometric Frobenius acts on the summand H^{q−2a}(Z)(−a) as F_Z ⊗ q^a (untwisted). Λ = ℤ/ℓ^m, O_E/λ^m, O_E or E.
hypotheses: As in EDC.4/blowup-direct-images; for Galois and Frobenius statements X and Z are defined over k₀ and the cohomology is that of X_k, Z_k.
For cohomology over a non-separably-closed k₀ the decomposition is of Galois modules after base change to k.
proofSteps: Apply RΓ(X, −) to Rπ_*Λ_X̃ ≅ Λ_X ⊕ ⊕_a i_*Λ_Z(−a)[−2a] (EDC.4/blowup-direct-images): H^q(X̃) ≅ H^q(X) ⊕ ⊕_a H^{q−2a}(Z)(−a). This is the decomposition stated by EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7.

Retain the imported exceptional Gysin columns of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7. At the sheaf level EDC.4/blowup-direct-images identifies their exceptional restrictions as −ζ^a p^*; this supplies the comparison before applying any support functor. No second global blow-up decomposition is planned.

π_*π^* = id: π is proper birational between smooth schemes of the same dimension, so π^!Λ_X ≅ Λ_X̃ by smooth purity on both sides (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6) and the trace defines π_*; π_*1 = 1 because π is an isomorphism over a dense open, and the projection formula (§F.2.7) gives π_*π^*x = x ∪ π_*1 = x.

Traces: Tr_X̃ = Tr_X ∘ π_* (composition of smooth traces, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11) and π_*π^* = id. Equivariance and Frobenius as in EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (d): ζ and the Gysin map of E are defined over k₀ and j_* raises the twist by one.
acceptance: Blowing up a k-rational point x on a smooth projective surface S over separably closed k (c = 2): H²(S̃) = H²(S) ⊕ Λ(−1)·[E] with [E]² = −1, H¹, H³ unchanged; if the surface and the point descend to 𝔽_q, the new geometric Frobenius eigenvalue is q. Checked independently of any Weil bound (the stage's acceptance test).
Blowing up a point in P³ (c = 3): b₂ and b₄ both increase by one, b_odd unchanged.
Euler characteristic: χ(X̃) = χ(X) + (c − 1)χ(Z); for c = 1 nothing changes.

sources.match: Weil I uses the blow-up formula along the smooth codimension-two centre A ∩ X: H*(X̃) = H*(X) ⊕ H^{*−2}(A ∩ X)(−1).
Milne obtains H*(X*) ≅ H*(X) ⊕ H*−2(A ∩ X)(−1) from the degenerating Leray spectral sequence of the blow-up.

§F.7 states the blow-up decomposition of RΓ and RΓ_c for a smooth centre with exceptional Gysin maps and their inverse signs, over an arbitrary field, with finite or ℓ-adic coefficients; its checks include the exceptional curve of square −1. The decomposition, explicit columns and inverse signs are imported; this node records the proper-trace retraction, support functoriality and Frobenius weights.

nodes.title: Cohomology of the blow-up along the axis of a pencil
nodes.statement: Let X ⊂ P^N be a smooth projective k-scheme of pure dimension n + 1 over a separably closed field k (ℓ invertible), and A ⊂ P^N a linear subspace of codimension 2 meeting X transversally, so that A ∩ X is smooth of pure codimension 2 in X (possibly empty). Let π : X̃ = Bl_{A∩X}X → X. Then for Λ = ℤ/ℓ^m, ℤ_ℓ, ℚ_ℓ: H^q(X̃, Λ) ≅ H^q(X, Λ) ⊕ H^{q−2}(A ∩ X, Λ)(−1), via π^* and j_*p^*, with π^* split injective; if X and A are defined over 𝔽_q the decomposition commutes with the geometric Frobenius, which acts on the second summand as q·F_{A∩X}. In particular b_q(X̃) = b_q(X) + b_{q−2}(A ∩ X) and χ(X̃) = χ(X) + χ(A ∩ X). The identification of X̃ with the incidence variety of the pencil and the map X̃ → P¹ belong to LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.3 and are not used here.
hypotheses: X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1; A a codimension-2 linear subspace transverse to X (so A ∩ X is smooth of codimension 2).
n≥1, so the ambient dimension is at least two; the empty-axis case remains allowed.
proofSteps: This is EDC.4/blowup-formula with c = 2, Z = A ∩ X, E = P(N_{Z/X}) a P¹-bundle over Z, ζ⁰ = 1.
Frobenius on the summand: EDC.4/blowup-formula (twist (−1) contributes the factor q).
acceptance: X = P² ⊂ P³ a plane (n + 1 = 2) and A a line meeting it transversally in one point x: X̃ = Bl_x P², b₂(X̃) = 1 + 1 = 2.

nodes.title: Pullback along blow-ups and projective bundles is split injective
nodes.statement: Let σ : X' → X be either (i) the blow-up of a smooth k-scheme X along a smooth closed subscheme Z of pure codimension c ≥ 2, or (ii) a projective bundle P(E) → X of relative dimension r ≥ 1 over a qcqs X, with ℓ invertible. For Λ = ℤ/ℓ^m, O_E/λ^m, O_E or E, σ^* : H^q(X, Λ) → H^q(X', Λ) is split injective, with retraction π_* in case (i) and a ↦ σ_*(ξ^r ∪ −) in case (ii); the same holds for cohomology with compact supports and for cohomology with supports in a closed subset T ⊂ X and its preimage. In case (ii) the cokernel is the sum of H^{q−2j}(X, Λ)(−j) for 1≤j≤r; for r=1 this is H^{q−2}(X, Λ)(−1), and in case (i) the cokernel is ⊕_{a=1}^{c−1} H^{q−2a}(Z, Λ)(−a), so σ^* is bijective in degrees q < 2 (and an isomorphism in all degrees when Z = ∅).
hypotheses: As in EDC.4/blowup-formula (case (i)) or EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (case (ii)); integral coefficients O_E allowed.

The adic projective-bundle case has the finite-type and bounded-constructible range of EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition. Supports and compact supports use the same proper derived decomposition, not a new pullback on compact supports for arbitrary nonproper morphisms.

For compact supports assume X separated of finite type over a field, so RΓ_c is the supplied structural lower-shriek functor. The blow-up case retains that same geometric range from blowup-direct-images; the finite-coefficient ordinary/support projective-bundle statement keeps the qcqs range.

(ii) EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (a) and (c).

Compact supports and supports in T: apply the same decompositions of Rσ_*Λ (EDC.4/blowup-direct-images, EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (a)), which are isomorphisms in D(X, Λ), to RΓ_c(X, −) and RΓ_T(X, −); for σ proper, Rσ_! = Rσ_* (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.8, ClassicalAlgebraic.properSupports) and supports in the preimage of T are computed by the triangles of §0.7.

nodes.title: Vanishing and restricted subspaces of a hyperplane section, and primitive subspaces
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, ℓ invertible, E a field of coefficients (finite of characteristic ℓ, or finite over ℚ_ℓ), X a smooth projective k-scheme of pure dimension n + 1 and i : Y → X a smooth hyperplane section (pure dimension n), with Lefschetz class L = c₁(O_X(1)) ∈ H²(X, E(1)). Define the vanishing subspace Van(Y) := ker(i_* : H^n(Y, E) → H^{n+2}(X, E(1))) and the restricted subspace Res(Y) := im(i^* : H^n(X, E) → H^n(Y, E)), both E-subspaces of H^n(Y, E). Then, with respect to the Poincaré pairing ⟨y, y'⟩ = Tr_Y(y ∪ y') on H^n(Y, E) (perfect and (−1)^n-symmetric after the identification E(n) ≅ E over k), Res(Y) = Van(Y)^⊥ and Van(Y) = Res(Y)^⊥; dim Res(Y) + dim Van(Y) = dim H^n(Y). Moreover i_*i^* = L ∪ − on H^∗(X). For 0 ≤ q ≤ n + 1 the primitive subspace is P^q(X) := ker(L^{n+2−q} : H^q(X, E) → H^{2n+4−q}(X, E(n+2−q))). No decomposition H^n(Y) = Res(Y) ⊕ Van(Y) and no Lefschetz decomposition into primitive parts is asserted: both require hard Lefschetz (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9).
hypotheses: X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1 over k separably closed; Y a smooth hyperplane section; field coefficients E (so that orthogonal complements have complementary dimensions).
proofSteps: Van(Y) and Res(Y) are kernels and images of E-linear maps between finite-dimensional spaces (finiteness: EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.etaleFiniteness, for finite fields of coefficients; §§F.4.4–F.4.5 for ℓ-adic fields).

i_* is the transpose of i^* for the Poincaré pairings of Y and X (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6, Gysin maps and their projection formula): ⟨i^*x, y⟩_Y = ⟨x, i_*y⟩_X. Hence y ⊥ Res(Y) ⟺ i_*y ⊥ H^n(X) ⟺ i_*y = 0 (perfectness of Poincaré duality on X, §§F.5–F.6), i.e. Res(Y)^⊥ = Van(Y); the pairing on Y is perfect, so Van(Y)^⊥ = Res(Y) and the dimensions add up.
i_*i^*x = cl(Y) ∪ x = L ∪ x (projection formula of §F.6 and the agreement of the class of a Cartier divisor with the Kummer first Chern class, §0.9).
P^q(X) is a kernel of an E-linear map; nothing about its complement is claimed.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n: Van(Y) = 0 for n odd (H^n(Y) = 0) and for n even Van(Y) = 0 since i_* is an isomorphism H^n(P^n) → H^{n+2}(P^{n+1}); Res(Y) = H^n(Y).
Take X = P² with its O(3) Veronese embedding and Y a smooth plane cubic, which is a hyperplane section for that embedding. Then Res(Y)=0 and Van(Y)=H¹(Y), of dimension 2.

The intersection Res(Y) ∩ Van(Y) is not asserted to be 0: in characteristic ℓ coefficients E = 𝔽_2 and n even, the restricted class of a quadric hyperplane section can be isotropic; only orthogonality is proved.

The P²,O(3) test uses the actual Veronese embedding requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0. Orthogonality uses the actual restriction/Gysin maps, not arbitrary subspaces with matching dimensions.

nodes.title: Classical and pro-étale ℓ-adic constructible categories
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a field (or over ℤ[1/ℓ]-regular bases of dimension ≤ 1), ℓ invertible on X, E/ℚ_ℓ finite with ring of integers O and uniformizer λ. Imported, not planned here: for O = ℤ_ℓ, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.1–F.4.6 state the normalized bounded constructible ℓ-adic systems (VanishingCycles.normalizedAdicSystems), their classical realization K_ℤℓ = Rlim K_n (VanishingCycles.classicalAdicRealization), the comparison Rν_*K_pro ≅ K_ℤℓ with the pro-étale realization (VanishingCycles.etaleProetaleAdicComparison), integral finiteness and derived reduction (VanishingCycles.adicFiniteness), rational and finite-E realization through O_E lattices (VanishingCycles.rationalAdicRealization), and the passage of proper, smooth and Rf_! exchange, projection, tensor and Künneth through normalized systems (VanishingCycles.adicFunctoriality); §F.5 states adic duality as the realization of the finite-level duality. The node adds the λ-adic form for a possibly ramified O: the category D^b_c(X, O), obtained by taking the homotopy category of the normalized full subcategory of the enhanced coefficient-system limit of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E4.5, with K_m ∈ D_ctf(X, O/λ^m) and homotopy-coherent derived reduction equivalences (EDC.6/normalized-adic-system) is equivalent to Bhatt–Scholze's D_cons(X_proét, O) of derived λ-complete objects whose reductions are constructible, compatibly with the reduction functors K ↦ K ⊗^L O/λ^m. D^b_c(X, E) := D^b_c(X, O) ⊗ E is the full subcategory D_cons(X_proét, E), and D^b_c(X, Ē) is the 2-colimit over finite E'/E. Both carry the six operations f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, f^!, ⊗, RHom, compatible with the finite-level ones under reduction and with coefficient extension E → E'; for O = ℤ_ℓ these are the imported operations.
hypotheses: X of finite type over a field (or a regular base of dimension ≤ 1) with ℓ invertible; E/ℚ_ℓ finite.

For the six operations use the hypotheses of Bhatt–Scholze §§6.6–6.7 and Remark 6.8.15: noetherian finite-dimensional bases with ℓ invertible, and the quasi-excellence hypothesis of 6.7.1 for nonproper direct image. Completion and coefficient reconstruction on a replete topos are EnhancedDerivedSheaves E4 (§E4.5); constructibility, boundedness and the scheme six operations are additional inputs, not consequences of repleteness alone.

Tensor, internal Hom and coefficient change are the enhanced operations of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.3 in the ambient unbounded derived category; finite Tor amplitude is tested there against all degree-zero sheaves. Bounded outputs require actual bounded-constructible restriction witnesses. General-ring trace evaluation uses ctf inputs; bounded duality on every Dbc object uses its stated coefficient regime.
proofSteps: Pro-étale side: D(X_proét, O) and derived completion are EnhancedDerivedSheaves E4 (coefficient-system reconstruction, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/coefficient-system-reconstruction); D_cons is the subcategory of complete objects with constructible reductions (Bhatt–Scholze 6.5).

Use the enhanced limit and all higher coherence of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E4.5, taking its homotopy category only afterwards. The equivalence with λ-adic systems: K ↦ (K ⊗^L O/λ^m)_m with inverse Rlim (Bhatt–Scholze, comparison with Ekedahl's category; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/inverse-limit-reconstruction). For O = ℤ_ℓ this is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.2–F.4.3; for ramified O the same argument applies to the tower O/λ^m, since O/λ^{em} is a finite free ℤ/ℓ^m-algebra (e the ramification index) and the realization, its Milnor sequence and the pro-étale comparison only use the uniform bounds and the finite-level operations.

Six operations on D^b_c(X, O): defined levelwise on normalized systems by the finite-level operations of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.7–0.8, F.2 and F.5, which preserve D_ctf and commute with ⊗^L O/λ^m (projection formula, §F.2.7; finiteness, §F.3); E and Ē by localization and colimit (Bhatt–Scholze 6.8; for finite E also §F.4.5).
acceptance: X = Spec Ω, Ω separably closed: D^b_c(X, O) ≃ D^b_{fg}(O) and D^b_c(X, E) ≃ D^b_{fd}(E).
The constant system (O/λ^m)_m corresponds to O_X; its rationalization is E_X.

nodes.title: Transport of traces, duality and Gysin classes to ℓ-adic and rational coefficients
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, for X separated of finite type over a field k. Imported, not planned here: for O = ℤ_ℓ and for ℚ_ℓ and finite E, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5 states adic duality as the realization of finite-level duality, §F.6 the adic realizations of the smooth trace, purity and Gysin maps, §F.4.4 finite generation and derived reduction of geometric cohomology, and §F.4.5 rational tensor, Hom and duality. The node states these for a possibly ramified O = O_E and records the integral details used downstream: (a) the dualizing complex K_X := a^!O ∈ D^b_c(X, O) reduces to the finite-level K_X ⊗^L O/λ^m and D_X := RHom(−, K_X) preserves D^b_c(X, O); the evaluation K → D_XD_XK is an isomorphism for all K ∈ D^b_c(X, O) (its reductions have finite Tor amplitude over O/λ^m, so the imported ctf biduality applies levelwise and passes to the limit) and for D^b_c(X, E); D_X exchanges Rf_* and Rf_!, f^* and f^!. (b) The smooth trace Tr_f, the purity isomorphism f^!O ≅ O(d)[2d] for smooth f of relative dimension d, the Gysin maps and the cycle class map cl : CH^r(X) → H^{2r}(X, O(r)) are the limits of their finite-level versions, with integral torsion retained: for geometric cohomology (X over a separably closed field), H^q(X, O) = lim H^q(X, O/λ^m) is a finitely generated O-module whose torsion is not discarded, and the universal-coefficient sequences 0 → H^q(X, O) ⊗ O/λ^m → H^q(X, O/λ^m) → H^{q+1}(X, O)[λ^m] → 0 hold. (c) After ⊗E these give the rational statements, compatible with extension of scalars E → E' ⊂ Ē (D_X, traces and cycle classes commute with − ⊗_E E').
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over a field; ℓ invertible; O = O_E.

The inverse-limit, finite-generation and finite-group Mittag-Leffler assertions in (b) concern geometric cohomology over a separably closed field. Arbitrary-field arithmetic cohomology is not asserted finite. Cycle-class transport uses the perfect-field and cycle hypotheses of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/cycle-class-map, whose descent to Chow groups EtaleCohomologyFoundations does not state.
proofSteps: Use ambient coefficient reduction and the uniform ordinary/Tor bounds of the enhanced normalized systems for the bounded restrictions. O is a DVR of global dimension one: bounded constructible O-complexes are stratumwise perfect, and their derived reductions lie in D_ctf(X,O/λ^m) with a common interval. Apply exactly the ctf biduality and exchange isomorphisms of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5 at those levels; the dual systems retain common constructibility and bounds, and enhanced reconstruction gives integral biduality. Quotient-to-quotient reduction is not bounded on every Dbc object. No biduality on arbitrary nonperfect finite-level Dbc inputs is imported. Finite-group Mittag–Leffler is used only for geometric cohomology.

Traces, purity and Gysin maps are compatible with reduction by construction (their finite-level constructions in EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.9–0.11 and F.6 are natural in Λ), hence define maps of systems; cycle classes likewise (EDC.3/cycle-class-map).

Universal coefficients: RΓ(X, K) ⊗^L O/λ^m ≅ RΓ(X, K ⊗^L O/λ^m) for K ∈ D^b_c(X, O) and RΓ(X, K) ∈ D^b_{fg}(O) (for O = ℤ_ℓ this is §F.4.4; for ramified O the same argument over the tower O/λ^m). The finiteness clause is geometric; over arbitrary k the absolute Galois cohomology need not be finitely generated.
Coefficient extension: E' is finite free over E, so all operations commute with − ⊗_E E'.
acceptance: X smooth proper connected of dimension d over k separably closed: H^{2d}(X, O(d)) ≅ O via the limit trace, and Poincaré duality over O has the Ext¹ correction of integral duality (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5, adic duality as the realization of §F.4).
An Enriques surface over k separably closed of characteristic ≠ 2 with ℓ = 2: H²(X, ℤ_2) has torsion ℤ/2, which the integral statement retains.

nodes.title: Perverse t-structures with ℓ-adic coefficients and coefficient extension
nodes.statement: For X of finite type over k (ℓ invertible) and E/ℚ_ℓ finite, the middle perverse t-structure of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure on D^b_c(X, E) and on D^b_c(X, Ē) := 2-colim_{E'} D^b_c(X, E') is compatible with coefficient extension: for a finite extension E ⊂ E', K ↦ K ⊗_E E' is t-exact, induces an exact functor Perv(X, E) → Perv(X, E'), commutes with j_!* and IC (IC_X(L) ⊗_E E' ≅ IC_X(L ⊗_E E')), and Hom_{Perv(X,E')}(K ⊗ E', L ⊗ E') = Hom_{Perv(X,E)}(K, L) ⊗_E E'. Reduction from O to O/λ (K ↦ K ⊗^L O/λ) is right t-exact for p and sends the heart of p to pD^{[−1,0]} (EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity). Simple objects of Perv(X, Ē) are defined over some finite E'.
hypotheses: X of finite type over a field, ℓ invertible; E ⊂ E' finite extensions of ℚ_ℓ.

The perverse t-structures are those of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure (stated upstream as VanishingCycles.fieldPerverseTStructure, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8, for finite and ℓ-adic coefficients). The Hom scalar-extension identity is for a finite coefficient-field extension (general algebraic extensions through the stated filtered colimit), not an arbitrary field homomorphism.
proofSteps: Faithfully flat finite scalar extension commutes with stalks and costalks and is exact, hence perverse t-exact. nodes.title: Comparison with the complex-analytic constructible category
nodes.statement: Let X be separated of finite type over ℂ, X^an its analytification and Λ a finite ring (killed by n), O_E or E. Imported from ComplexComparisonPartII §§C6.3–C6.6: finite ordinary and compact Artin comparison, proper Rf_* exchange, separated Rf_! exchange on ctf inputs, and normalized ℤ_ℓ/ℚ_ℓ topological realization. The residue here is the categorical and perverse form, ramified O_E coefficients, the rational essential image, and the additional nonproper Rf_* exchange requested below. The comparison functor ε^* : D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) → D^b_c(X^an, Λ) (constructible for algebraic stratifications) is an equivalence for finite Λ (BBD 6.1.2, from Artin's comparison theorem SGA 4 XVI 4.1), commutes with f^*, Rf_*, Rf_! and f^! in their constructible ranges for morphisms of finite type. Tensor and RHom comparison are stated in the ambient unbounded categories: for bounded constructible K,L, finite Tor amplitude of K gives bounded-constructible restriction receipts for K⊗^L L and RHom(K,L), and the comparisons then restrict through these receipts. Bounded Verdier duality on every Dbc object is asserted only for the finite-field, DVR-quotient, integral and rational coefficient regimes; for a general finite ring it uses the existing ctf input range. The functor is t-exact for the middle perverse t-structures, so it identifies Perv(X_ét, Λ) with algebraically constructible perverse sheaves on X^an and preserves j_!* and IC. For O_E coefficients the corresponding equivalence follows from finite-level comparison. For E coefficients the functor is fully faithful with essential image the algebraically constructible complexes whose cohomology local systems on normal connected strata admit monodromy-stable O_E lattices (BBD 6.1.2(A″),(B″)); it is an equivalence onto that image; the comparison of trace maps and cycle classes with topological orientation classes is EDC.6/trace-orientation-comparison.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; algebraically constructible complexes; Λ finite, O_E or E.

For E coefficients the analytic target is restricted to the monodromy-stable-lattice essential image. A rank-one E local system on ℂ× with monodromy ℓ admits no stable O_E lattice and is not the analytification of an étale E local system.

Tensor and internal-Hom outputs are first ambient objects. A bounded output is corestricted only with its actual bounded-constructible witness; the displayed comparisons use finite-Tor first input. Analytic complex-field tensor/RHom used by geometric-origin constructors has separate field-coefficient boundedness receipts.
proofSteps: Import analytification and the finite/adic ordinary and compact comparisons from ComplexComparisonPartII §§C−1.1,C6.0–C6.6 (TauCetiRoadmap #848, head d6cb0fc). Its generic enhanced analytic categories use EnhancedDerivedSheaves §§0.1–0.4. It already supplies proper Rf_* and separated Rf_! exchange on ctf inputs. Request only the remaining nonproper constructible Rf_* comparison through SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2. BBD 6.1.2, pp.148–151 supplies the categorical refinement: finite and integral equivalences and rational full faithfulness with the stable-lattice essential image. Apply the finite comparisons levelwise to the coherent λ-adic systems for ramified O_E.

For the finite non-ctf coefficient range, use BBD 6.1.2(C),(C′),(C″), pp.148–151 and its localization/dévissage argument to extend the operation comparison beyond the imported ctf exchange. Compare the ambient tensor and RHom of the realized inputs; finite-Tor boundedness receipts and realization isomorphisms identify the bounded restrictions. nodes.title: Algebraic traces and cycle classes versus topological orientation
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth separated of pure dimension d over ℂ and Λ = ℤ/n, ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ. Under the comparison isomorphism H^q(X_ét, Λ) ≅ H^q(X^an, Λ) (EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison) and the identification Λ(1) ≅ Λ given by exp(2πi/n) ↦ 1 (ζ_n ↦ 1): (a) the étale trace Tr : H^{2d}_c(X_ét, Λ(d)) → Λ (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11) corresponds to integration against the complex orientation, Tr_X ↦ ∫_{X^an}, sending the class of a point to 1; (b) the étale cycle class cl(Z) ∈ H^{2r}(X_ét, Λ(r)) of a closed subvariety of codimension r corresponds to the topological fundamental class of Z^an (Poincaré dual of [Z^an]); (c) cup products and compactly supported duality pairings correspond. The sign convention: c₁(O(1)) on P¹ maps to the positive generator of H²(P¹(ℂ), ℤ) for the complex orientation, with the Kummer sequence matched to the exponential sequence by exp(2πi·/n).
hypotheses: X smooth over ℂ; the identification Λ(1) ≅ Λ through e^{2πi/n} is part of the statement (other choices change Tr by a sign or a unit).
proofSteps: Use the analytic Kummer sequence and exp(2πi·) with the same positive root-of-unity coordinates. The Kummer connecting cocycle is the exponential integral Chern cocycle modulo n. ComplexComparisonPartII §C5.4 already identifies the integral analytic class with the topological c₁, and §C6.3 fixes the positive Kummer generator on G_m. The residue here is the commutative Kummer/exponential connecting square and its trace/Gysin normalization, as in BBD 6.1.4, pp.151–152.

Traces are normalized by points and c₁(O(1)) on P¹ (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11, ClassicalAlgebraic.smoothTrace, whose P¹ check sends c₁(O(1)) to 1), and the topological integration satisfies the same normalization; both are compatible with Gysin maps of points, so they agree.

Cycle classes: both sides are determined by the fundamental class of the smooth locus and semi-purity (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/cycle-class-map; the localized classes of regular immersions are EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9).
acceptance: X = P¹: Tr(c₁(O(1))) = 1 on both sides (the stage's acceptance: P¹'s orientation).
X a connected smooth open curve: H²_c(X, Λ(1)) ≅ Λ with the same normalization.
A smooth divisor D ⊂ X: cl(D) = c₁(O(D)) maps to the topological Poincaré dual of [D] under both routes.

nodes.title: Betti numbers of smooth complete intersections are independent of the field
nodes.statement: Fix N, m and a multidegree (d_1, …, d_{N−m}). For every separably closed field k of characteristic ≠ ℓ and every smooth complete intersection X ⊂ P^N_k of that multidegree and dimension m, every Betti number is independent of the geometric field, and dim H^m(X, ℚ_ℓ) equals the topological Betti number b_m(X_ℂ^an) of any smooth complete intersection X_ℂ ⊂ P^N_ℂ of the same multidegree, and hence the primitive rank b_m^0 = dim H^m(X, ℚ_ℓ)_0 of EDC.4/complete-intersection-cohomology is a function of (N, m, d_•) only; for a smooth hypersurface of degree d, b_m^0 = ((d − 1)^{m+2} + (−1)^m(d − 1))/d.
hypotheses: Smooth complete intersections of a fixed multidegree; ℓ invertible in k.
m≥1 for the primitive-rank and displayed hypersurface formula, as in EDC.4/complete-intersection-cohomology; d≥1. Zero-dimensional reduced cohomology is a different convention.
proofSteps: The parameter scheme S ⊂ ∏ P(Sym^{d_i}) over Spec ℤ[1/ℓ] of tuples defining a smooth complete intersection of dimension m is open with geometrically irreducible (hence connected) fibres and nonempty over every point; the universal family f : 𝒳 → S is smooth and proper (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0).

Smooth proper base change makes R^mf_*ℚ_ℓ lisse on the connected parameter scheme (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.lisseDirectImageTransport, at finite levels, then §F.4), hence its rank is constant. Identifications of different geometric fibres require a choice of path or specialization data; the canonical conclusion here is equality of ranks, not a canonical identification of all fibres.

Over ℂ, Artin's comparison (EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison) identifies dim H^m(X_ℂ, ℚ_ℓ) with the topological Betti number. The hypersurface formula: by étale Gauss–Bonnet (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6, VanishingCycles.etaleGaussBonnet) χ(X) = deg c_m(T_X), and c(T_X) = (1+h)^{N+1}∏(1+d_ih)^{−1} restricted to X (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5); EDC.4/complete-intersection-cohomology gives all other Betti numbers, so b_m is determined by χ.
acceptance: Smooth plane cubics: b_1 = 2 over every k (= (8 − 2)/3 = 2 by the formula with m = 1, d = 3).
Smooth quadric surfaces: b_2^0 = (1 + 1)/2 = 1.

sources.match: Milne: the primitive rank depends only on m and the degrees, with the explicit hypersurface formula.

§F.3 states lissity of R^if_* for smooth proper f with finite lisse coefficients; §F.6 states étale Gauss–Bonnet deg c_d(T_X) = Σ(−1)^i dim H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ) for smooth proper X over an algebraically closed field.

nodes.title: Transport of duality and perversity statements to diamonds in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let k be of characteristic p, X separated of finite type over k, and Λ torsion killed by an integer prime to p. Put a : X → Spec k, B = (Spec k)^◇, and K_{X^◇/B} = a^{◇!}c_{Spec k}^*Λ. For K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ), ECD 27.2–27.4 imply Rc_{X*}K_{X^◇/B} ≅ K_X and Rc_{X*}RHom(c_X^*K, K_{X^◇/B}) ≅ D_XK. These recover scheme duality through the right adjoint. The stronger assertions c_X^*K_X ≅ K_{X^◇/B} and c_X^*D_XK ≅ D_{X^◇/B}c_X^*K are conditional on an additional exceptional-pullback/internal-Hom comparison and preservation of the essential image; these inputs are not supplied by 27.1–27.4. No perverse t-structure on arbitrary diamonds is asserted.
hypotheses: Characteristic p, finite-type separated X over k, torsion coefficients prime to p; the dualizing complex is relative to B = (Spec k)^◇.
The strong pullback transport requested by the stage remains a recorded gap; this node proves only right-adjoint recovery.

The Rc_* identities live in the unbounded etale derived category. A bounded constructible K enters through its etale realization; no preservation of D^b_c by Rc_* on arbitrary diamond objects is assumed. The relative dualizing objects on both sides use their actual maps to the common base.

Tensor, internal Hom and coefficient change are the enhanced operations of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.3 in the ambient unbounded derived category; the scheme dualizing complex, biduality and exchange isomorphisms are EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5. Bounded outputs require actual bounded-constructible restriction witnesses.
proofSteps: Use R a^! Rc_{Spec k*} ≅ Rc_{X*}R a^{◇!} and Rc_{Spec k*}c_{Spec k}^*Λ ≅ Λ to recover K_X.
Apply the internal-Hom right-adjoint identity of 27.3 with first input c_X^*K, then the unit K ≅ Rc_{X*}c_X^*K to obtain D_XK.
A counit c_X^*Rc_{X*}D_{X^◇/B}c_X^*K → D_{X^◇/B}c_X^*K need not be an isomorphism by full faithfulness alone; the missing essential-image argument is recorded as a gap.

For X=P¹, right-adjoint recovery gives Λ(1)[2]. Strong c^* transport on either example remains conditional on the additional L3 theorem; these checks assert no unconditional counit isomorphism.

nodes.title: Uniformly bounded constructible normalized adic systems
nodes.statement: For a complete DVR O as in the coefficient conventions, write R_n=O/λ^(n+1). Import Sys_O as the limit in enhanced stable categories of D(X_ét,R_n) under derived coefficient reduction (EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E4.5). Equivalently, use its coCartesian-section description: levels, reduction equivalences, all higher associator coherences and homotopy-coherent maps. A list of level isomorphisms with only identity and triple equations in the triangulated homotopy categories is insufficient. Define the normalized full subcategory by requiring each level bounded constructible, a single ordinary interval and Tor interval valid at every level (Tor tested against all degree-zero ambient R_n-sheaves), and one finite algebraic stratification with all level cohomology sheaves lisse finite. NormalizedSystem is the homotopy category of this enhanced full subcategory; take the homotopy category after the enhanced limit. Reduction is ambient derived tensor, corestricted to bounded objects only through these witnesses. For O=ℤ_ℓ the uniform-bounds system is imported from EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.1; the residue is the ramified tower and the common-stratification API. No unrestricted triangulated inverse limit is declared constructible.
hypotheses: X is a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with ℓ invertible; O is the ring of integers in a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, with uniformizer λ. The geometric comparison and six-operation extensions retain their additional finite-type/base hypotheses from their respective nodes.
proofSteps: Use the enhanced coefficient diagram and its full homotopy-coherent limit of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E4.5, with tensor associators of §§0.3–0.4. Restrict it by the ordinary/Tor bounds and constructibility predicate; do not reconstruct its objects or morphisms from a 2-limit of homotopy categories. Its visible identity/triple comparisons are consequences of this full coherence, not the definition. All Tor and reduction tests occur in the unbounded ambient coefficient categories.

Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.6.11 (pp.49,54) identify constructibility with derived completeness and stratumwise perfect local models. For a noetherian finite-dimensional X these provide a common finite stratification and uniform bounds. The operations and their reduction compatibilities use Lemmas 6.7.13,6.7.18–6.7.20 (pp.57–58), with rational passage in 6.8.14–6.8.15 (pp.61–62). E4 reconstruction gives completeness, not constructibility by itself.
The normalization equivalence identifies every level with derived coefficient reduction; for O = ℤ_ℓ this is the comparison of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.1–F.4.3.

Over O, which has global dimension one, integral-to-quotient reduction of a bounded constructible complex has a bounded realization. Quotient-to-quotient reduction does not have this property on all Dbc objects. On a separably closed point, R = ℤ/ℓ² and M = R/ℓ have Tor_i(M, M) = M and Ext^i(M, M) = M for every i ≥ 0; the periodic multiplication-by-ℓ free resolution proves the obstruction (compare the Tor check of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.1). M remains in Dbc and in the point perverse heart, but has no finite Tor amplitude.

Use the coefficient-module sheaf category for the specified regime: finite levels have the t-exact native étale identification, while integral and rational objects realize in the pro-étale completed-coefficient category (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.3). Neither faithful realization nor its t-compatibility is asserted for ordinary étale constant-O sheaves.
acceptance: The reduction functors and their composition transformations are those of the imported enhanced limit; passing to its homotopy category preserves them without replacing the system by a list of pairwise isomorphisms.

Agreement with the upstream notion: for O = ℤ_ℓ a system is normalized exactly when it is a normalized system in the sense of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.1 whose levels admit one common lisse stratification; the constant tower is normalized there and here.

conventions: Unless a target explicitly gives a broader finite-coefficient scope, schemes in the geometric targets are separated and of finite type over a specified field k. The suggested file retains only native linear-algebra models and the three pinned affine-geometry declarations; it does not construct geometric cohomology carriers.

Integral coefficients O are the ring of integers of a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ, with a chosen uniformizer λ; ℓ is prime and invertible in k. Finite coefficients have a positive annihilator invertible in k. Perverse coefficient regimes are finite ℓ-power torsion fields or DVR quotients, O, or finite E. The intended IntegralDatum and RationalDatum interfaces record these data in the reader; they are not admitted Lean carriers.
Cohomological shifts satisfy H^q(K[n]) = H^{q+n}(K). Geometric Frobenius acts on E(1) by q inverse (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.10.2b). Point and hyperplane trace classes have degree +1 (§0.11).

Projective bundles parametrize lines in V, with O(1) dual to the tautological line. Thus the Chern relation is the sum of c_r(V) xi^(m+1-r), with plus signs. Exceptional self-intersection is multiplication by minus zeta.

Every geometric declaration is a planning target with implementationStatus unchecked. Intended declaration names below specify the future API. The suggested file contains only real-bodied definitions on existing Mathlib types, native linear-algebra milestones and examples. Its admitted theorem bodies check elaboration only; the enhanced categories and geometric constructions remain reader targets.

Derived tensor, internal Hom and finite-level coefficient reduction are the enhanced operations of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.3 in the ambient unbounded coefficient category. Tor amplitude is tested there against every degree-zero coefficient sheaf. A bounded restriction is obtained from an actual bounded-constructible witness.

The intended ambient coefficient category is the unbounded enhanced derived category of the appropriate module sheaves, supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves §§0.1–0.4. Finite torsion coefficients use small-étale module sheaves and their t-exact pro-étale comparison. Integral and rational coefficients use completed coefficient sheaves O_X and E_X on the pro-étale site (Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.1–6.8.2, p.58; 6.8.15, p.62; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4). Ordinary étale constant-O sheaves do not model this category. Constructibility and completeness are conditions imported with the adic formalism.
